newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA C.BANK PROTESTS AGAINST RUSSIAN TAX POLICE.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA C.BANK PROTESTS AGAINST RUSSIAN TAX POLICE.

text.p: Latvian central bank president Einar Repshe on Wednesday criticised Russian tax police after several bank accounts of Latvian, Lithuanian and Estonian banks were frozen in St Petersburg.
Local media have reported that several Baltic banks had their correspondent accounts blocked by the tax police for non-payment of tax. The number of banks is not yet known.

"The president (Repshe) considers that the action of the tax inspectorate of the Russian Federation to block the correspondent accounts of Baltic banks in St Petersburg is unprecented and may negatively influence the economic relations of Latvia and Russia," the central bank said in a statement.
"The action of the tax police of St Petersburg may have far-reaching and negative effects on economic cooperation between the Baltic states and Russia," the statement said.
Estonian banks Forekspank, Tallinna Pank and EVEA Pank all said they had accounts frozen.

"We are trying to find out the principles of the decision and who it affects but we do not have enough information yet," Kaija Kell, the information officer at the Estonian central bank, told Reuters.
The Lithuanian central bank said it thought that only two Lithuanian banks were affected, Snoras Bank and small regional bank, Siauliu.
"The central bank is considering how to solve the problem although the amounts are not so big and will not affect banking activities," a central bank spokesman said.
